tour.welcome: Hi! Glad you're here. Let me walk you through the basics. Sound good?
tour.personnel: Nothing happens without a team. Hire at least one engineer first.
tour.hardwareDev: Now the core business: in the "Development" tab you build your computer models. Pick a CPU, RAM, case and target segment (Gamer, Office, Workstation). Higher specs = higher price, but also higher dev cost.
tour.marketing: Great products need to be heard of. For a start I suggest {{amount}} marketing budget.
tour.development: Active developments speed up with budget. Try {{amount}} per quarter — your models hit the market sooner.
tour.research: Research pays off long term. {{amount}} is a solid starting point. R&D unlocks exclusive parts the competition doesn't have yet.
tour.supportBudget: Don't forget support! A support specialist plus budget protects your reputation and brings customers back. No support means returns, bad reviews, and falling sales.
tour.moreRoles: You need more than engineers. Hire a marketer (boosts marketing impact), a researcher (speeds up R&D) and a support specialist. Each role raises the efficiency cap of its budget area.
tour.competition: The "Market" tab shows your rivals and their models. Watch prices, specs and market share. Find the gap — weak price/performance from a competitor is your opening.
tour.quarterAdvance: When you're done, end the quarter (top right). Sales get simulated, salaries paid, research progresses — and you'll see the quarterly report.
tour.financingIntro: Last but not least: three ways to finance your growth — pick wisely, each has its price.
tour.financingBootstrap: 1) Bootstrap: Grow from cashflow. Safe but slow. Classic mid-tech play.
tour.financingLoan: 2) Bank loan: Cash against interest (7–11% in the 80s). Bank only lends when you can show revenue.
tour.financingVc: 3) VC pitch: Big money for equity. Pitch to LLM-driven investors — convince them and you bag $3–5M for your moonshot.
tour.wrapUp: That's it for the basics. Situational tips will pop up automatically in the "Tips" tab. And I'm always one click away in chat. Good luck out there!
